Then reason: the question stem says that after the obliquity of the ecliptic becomes 0°, the climate type of place A can no longer be found on Earth, indicating that this kind of climate depends on the seasonal movement of pressure belts and wind belts to form. The typical climate that fits this feature is the Mediterranean climate, which is distributed on the west coasts of continents between about 30°–40° latitude. In the figure, A is below the 40° line: if this 40° line is 40°N in the Northern Hemisphere, then A is located south of 40°N, possibly on the west coast of a continent at 30°–40°N, which conforms to the distribution of the Mediterranean climate; if it is 40°S in the Southern Hemisphere, then A is south of 40°S, with a relatively high latitude, and does not conform to the typical distribution of the Mediterranean climate. Therefore, place A is actually located in the Northern Hemisphere.

Then reason: the question stem says that after the obliquity of the ecliptic becomes 0°, the climate type of place A can no longer be found on Earth, indicating that this kind of climate depends on the seasonal movement of pressure belts and wind belts to form. The typical climate that fits this feature is the Mediterranean climate, which is distributed on the west coasts of continents between about 30°–40° latitude. In the figure, A is below the 40° line: if this 40° line is 40°N in the Northern Hemisphere, then A is located south of 40°N, possibly on the west coast of a continent at 30°–40°N, which conforms to the distribution of the Mediterranean climate; if it is 40°S in the Southern Hemisphere, then A is south of 40°S, with a relatively high latitude, and does not conform to the typical distribution of the Mediterranean climate. Therefore, place A is actually located in the Northern Hemisphere.
